# Cartesia cookbook

> Templates and recipes for Cartesia speech and voice agents: Sonic text to speech, Ink speech to text and Managed Agents in Next.js, Python, Node and Expo. Each template is a standalone folder in examples/ with a README, an AGENTS.md for coding agents and an .env.example.

Current facts (from facts.json): text to speech model `sonic-3.6`, streaming speech to text with turn detection `ink-2` (en, es, fr, hi, ja), file speech to text `ink-whisper`, API version header `Cartesia-Version: 2026-08-14`. Any other Sonic model id is sunset (the last ones stopped working on 2026-10-20) or a deprecated alias. The API key stays on the server; browsers and apps get a 60 second access token from a server route (`client.accessToken.create({ grants, expires_in: 60 })`). SDKs: `@cartesia/cartesia-js` (TypeScript) and `cartesia` (Python).

Clone one template: `npx degit cartesia-ai/cookbook/examples/<name> <name>`. Node template READMEs give npm commands; pnpm works too. Python templates use uv. Feature tags: word-timestamps, turn-detection, barge-in, multilingual, telephony, client-tools, batch-stt, voice-cloning.

## Templates

- [Voice chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/voice-chat/README.md): Talk to a Cartesia Managed Agent in the browser, interrupt it mid-sentence, and watch the transcript update as it speaks. Features: turn-detection, barge-in. Stack: Next.js 16, React 19, shadcn/ui, agents-web. Models: ink-2, sonic-3.6. Agent notes: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/voice-chat/AGENTS.md
- [Front desk](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/front-desk/README.md): An AI phone receptionist on a Cartesia Managed Agent that answers calls, books appointments, takes messages and logs every call with transcript and latency. Features: telephony, client-tools. Stack: Python, FastAPI, htmx, SQLite, uv. Models: ink-2, sonic-3.6. Agent notes: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/front-desk/AGENTS.md
- [Coding voice mode](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/coding-voice-mode/README.md): Talk to Claude Code, Cursor or Codex through one MCP tool: Sonic 3.6 speaks the agent's message and Ink 2 turn detection hears your reply. Features: turn-detection, multilingual. Stack: Python, FastMCP, sounddevice, uv. Models: sonic-3.6, ink-2. Agent notes: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/coding-voice-mode/AGENTS.md
- [Pocket interpreter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/pocket-interpreter/README.md): Real-time voice translation between two people on one phone: Ink 2 hears each turn, an LLM translates it, and Sonic 3.6 speaks it. Features: turn-detection, multilingual. Stack: Next.js 16, React 19, AI SDK, Web Audio, shadcn/ui. Models: ink-2, sonic-3.6. Agent notes: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/pocket-interpreter/AGENTS.md
- [Ebook to audiobook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/audiobook/README.md): Turn an EPUB into narrated MP3 chapters with Sonic 3.6, a voice per speaker, and word timestamps for read-along. Features: word-timestamps. Stack: Python, Gradio, EbookLib, ffmpeg, uv. Models: sonic-3.6. Agent notes: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/audiobook/AGENTS.md
- [Docs voice widget](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/docs-voice-widget/README.md): Add a voice agent to any documentation site with one script tag. It answers from your docs, cites the page and scrolls to the section. Features: turn-detection, barge-in, client-tools, multilingual. Stack: Hono, Node.js, Web Components, esbuild, BM25 or OpenAI embeddings. Models: ink-2, sonic-3.6. Agent notes: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/docs-voice-widget/AGENTS.md
- [Speaking partner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/speaking-partner/README.md): Practice a language out loud in role plays with a Cartesia Managed Agent, with written corrections after every line. Features: turn-detection, barge-in, client-tools, multilingual. Stack: Next.js 16, React 19, AI SDK, shadcn/ui, agents-web. Models: ink-2, sonic-3.6. Agent notes: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/speaking-partner/AGENTS.md
- [Article to podcast](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/article-to-podcast/README.md): Paste a link or text and get a two-host podcast episode voiced by Sonic 3.6, with a transcript that follows along. Features: multilingual. Stack: Next.js 16, React 19, AI SDK, Mozilla Readability, shadcn/ui. Models: sonic-3.6. Agent notes: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/article-to-podcast/AGENTS.md
- [Meeting notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/meeting-notes/README.md): Transcribe meetings with ink-whisper and get a summary and action items. Notes are stored in the browser. Audio goes to Cartesia and the transcript to your LLM. Features: batch-stt, multilingual. Stack: Next.js 16, React 19, AI SDK, IndexedDB, shadcn/ui. Models: ink-whisper. Agent notes: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/meeting-notes/AGENTS.md
- [Voice journal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/voice-journal/README.md): An Expo voice diary for iOS, Android and the web: ink-whisper transcribes each entry and Sonic 3.6 reads a weekly recap aloud. Features: batch-stt. Stack: Expo, React Native, Expo Router API routes, AI SDK, AsyncStorage. Models: ink-whisper, sonic-3.6. Agent notes: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/voice-journal/AGENTS.md
- [Story time](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/story-time/README.md): An interactive story app where Sonic 3.6 voices every character with word highlighting and you choose what happens next, by tap or by voice with Ink 2. Features: word-timestamps, turn-detection. Stack: Next.js 16, React 19, AI SDK, IndexedDB, shadcn/ui. Models: sonic-3.6, ink-2. Agent notes: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/examples/story-time/AGENTS.md

## Recipes: Guides

- [Use Cartesia from the browser without exposing your API key](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/00-guides/01-browser-auth-with-access-tokens.mdx): Keep your API key on the server and give the browser a token that expires in 60 seconds.

## Recipes: Next.js

- [Stream text to speech in Next.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/01-next/01-stream-speech.mdx): Stream Sonic audio through a route handler and play it in the browser while it is still being generated.
- [Turn an article into a podcast in Next.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/01-next/02-article-to-podcast.mdx): Fetch an article, have a model write a two-host script, voice each line with Sonic 3.6, and play one episode with a synced transcript.
- [Transcribe and summarize meetings in Next.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/01-next/20-transcribe-and-summarize-meetings.mdx): Record audio in the browser, transcribe it with ink-whisper, and turn the transcript into a summary, decisions and action items.
- [Narrate a story with a different voice per character and highlight each word](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/01-next/30-multi-voice-narration-with-word-timestamps.mdx): Read a story aloud with Cartesia Sonic 3.6 text to speech, one voice per character, highlight each word from Sonic's word timestamps, and hear a spoken choice with Ink 2 speech to text, in Next.js.
- [Build a real-time two-way voice translator with Ink 2 and Sonic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/01-next/40-real-time-voice-translation.mdx): Translate a spoken conversation between two people on one phone with Cartesia Ink 2 streaming speech to text, an LLM, and Sonic 3.6 text to speech in Next.js.

## Recipes: Node.js

- [Convert text to speech and save a WAV file in Node](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/05-node/01-generate-speech-to-file.mdx): Turn text into a WAV file with a short Node script.
- [Stream text to speech from an LLM token stream](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/05-node/02-stream-llm-text-to-speech.mdx): Push LLM tokens into a Cartesia Sonic 3.6 WebSocket context as they arrive (continuations), so speech starts before the model finishes writing, in Node with the AI SDK.
- [Get word timestamps from Sonic text to speech](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/05-node/03-word-timestamps.mdx): Ask Cartesia Sonic 3.6 for word-level timestamps with add_timestamps, collect them from the SSE stream in Node, and use them for captions, read-along highlighting or barge-in.
- [Stream speech to text in real time with Ink 2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/05-node/04-real-time-speech-to-text.mdx): Send live audio to Cartesia Ink 2 over the turns WebSocket in Node and get partial transcripts plus turn.start and turn.end events, with no separate voice activity detector.

## Recipes: Python

- [Convert text to speech and save a WAV file in Python](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/10-python/01-generate-speech-to-file.mdx): Turn text into a WAV file with a short Python script.
- [Transcribe an audio file with ink-whisper in Python](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/10-python/02-transcribe-an-audio-file.mdx): Send a recorded audio file to Cartesia speech to text with the ink-whisper model in Python and get the transcript, its duration and word timestamps back.
- [Clone a voice from a short recording in Python](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/10-python/03-clone-a-voice.mdx): Create an instant voice clone from a 10 to 60 second clip with the Cartesia API in Python, speak with it through Sonic 3.6, and delete it when you are done.
- [Add voice mode to Claude Code, Cursor or Codex](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/10-python/05-voice-mode-for-coding-agents.mdx): Talk to Claude Code, Cursor or Codex with Sonic 3.6 speech out and Ink 2 turn detection in, through one MCP tool.
- [Turn an EPUB ebook into an audiobook with Python](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/10-python/10-ebook-to-audiobook.mdx): Narrate an EPUB with Sonic, a voice per speaker, and save word timestamps for read-along.

## Recipes: Agents

- [Connect to a Cartesia Managed Agent from the browser](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/15-agents/01-talk-to-a-managed-agent.mdx): Mint an agent token on the server and open the Managed Agents WebSocket from the browser.
- [Build a browser voice chat with a Managed Agent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/15-agents/02-voice-chat.mdx): Talk to a Cartesia Managed Agent in the browser with barge-in and streaming agent captions in Next.js, plus a variant with your own LLM, Ink 2 and Sonic 3.6.
- [Build an AI language speaking partner with a Managed Agent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/15-agents/03-speaking-partner.mdx): Practice speaking a language with a Cartesia Managed Agent and get written corrections after every line, using Next.js.
- [Add voice search to your docs with a Managed Agent and client tools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/15-agents/04-voice-search-for-your-docs.mdx): Add a one script tag voice widget to a docs site that answers from your pages with a Cartesia Managed Agent (ink-2 and sonic-3.6), cites the section and scrolls to it, using a web component and a Hono server.

## Recipes: Telephony

- [Build an AI receptionist that answers the phone and books appointments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/20-telephony/01-ai-receptionist-that-books-appointments.mdx): Put a Cartesia Managed Agent (Ink 2 speech to text, an LLM, Sonic 3.6 text to speech) on a phone number and give it booking tools served by a Python FastAPI app.

## Recipes: Mobile

- [Record and transcribe voice notes in an Expo app with ink-whisper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/content/cookbook/25-mobile/01-voice-notes-in-expo.mdx): Record a voice note with expo-audio, transcribe it with Cartesia ink-whisper speech to text through an Expo Router API route, and read a recap back with Sonic 3.6 text to speech on iOS, Android and the web.

## Repo files

- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/AGENTS.md): Repo rules for coding agents, commands, and a docs index.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): Repo layout, how templates share code, and how to add a template or recipe.
- [facts.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/facts.json): Current model ids, API version and retired ids. CI fails when a file drifts from it.
- [templates.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/templates.json): Every template with its env keys, models, features, Cartesia APIs, clone command and deploy link.
- [Agents web client](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/packages/agents-web/README.md): Browser client for the Managed Agents WebSocket that several templates copy.
- [Design rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cartesia-ai/cookbook/main/packages/kit/DESIGN.md): Layout, type and color rules every template UI follows.

## Cartesia docs

- [Sonic 3.6](https://docs.cartesia.ai/build-with-cartesia/tts-models/latest.md): Current text to speech model, snapshots and languages.
- [Ink 2](https://docs.cartesia.ai/build-with-cartesia/stt/latest.md): Current streaming speech to text model.
- [Older STT models](https://docs.cartesia.ai/build-with-cartesia/stt/older-models.md): ink-whisper, used for file (batch) transcription.
- [Deprecated models](https://docs.cartesia.ai/build-with-cartesia/tts-models/api-changes.md): Sunset dates and what replaces each old model.
- [Authenticate your applications](https://docs.cartesia.ai/get-started/authenticate-your-client-applications.md): Access tokens for browsers and apps, API keys on servers.
- [Client libraries](https://docs.cartesia.ai/tools/client-libraries.md): The TypeScript and Python SDKs.
- [Compare TTS endpoints](https://docs.cartesia.ai/use-the-api/compare-tts-endpoints.md): Bytes, SSE and WebSocket, and when to use each.
- [Compare STT endpoints](https://docs.cartesia.ai/use-the-api/stt/compare-endpoints.md): Batch, streaming and turn-detecting speech to text.
- [Turn detection](https://docs.cartesia.ai/use-the-api/stt/turns.md): Ink 2 turn events on /stt/turns/websocket.
- [Managed Agents](https://docs.cartesia.ai/agents/introduction.md): Create and run hosted voice agents.
- [Agents WebSocket API](https://docs.cartesia.ai/line/integrations/websocket-api.md): Audio and events between your app and a Managed Agent. The /line/ prefix is a legacy path; the page covers Managed Agents, not the Line SDK.
- [Client tools](https://docs.cartesia.ai/agents/client-tools.md): Run functions in your app during a call.
- [Phone numbers](https://docs.cartesia.ai/line/integrations/telephony/phone-numbers.md): Connect a number to an agent.
- [Pricing](https://docs.cartesia.ai/pricing.md): How Cartesia charges for usage.

## Optional

- [Cartesia docs index](https://docs.cartesia.ai/llms.txt): Every docs page as Markdown.
- [Cartesia agent skills](https://github.com/cartesia-ai/skills): Install with `npx skills add cartesia-ai/skills`.
